notes.summary:
Direct speech gives the exact words inside quotation marks: Rohan said, “I am tired.” Indirect (reported) speech reports the meaning without quotation marks: Rohan said that he was tired.

SSC gives one sentence and asks for its indirect form (sometimes the direct form). You usually get 1 question in Tier 1 and 1 to 3 in Tier 2. Every conversion makes up to five changes: the reporting verb, the connector, the pronouns, the tense and the time and place words. Wrong options get exactly one of these wrong, so check them in that order.

concepts.title: The five changes
concepts.body:
1. Reporting verb: said stays said if there is no listener; said to + person becomes told + person. Questions take asked / enquired; commands take ordered / requested / advised.
  2. Connector: statements take that; yes/no questions take if / whether; wh-questions keep their question word; commands take to + V1.
  3. Pronouns: change them to fit the reporter (see the SON rule).
  4. Tense: if the reporting verb is past, move the reported verb one step back.
  5. Time and place words: now → then, today → that day, here → there.

Example: She said to me, “I will meet you here tomorrow.” → She told me that she would meet me there the next day.

concepts.title: Tense back-shift
concepts.body:
Apply this only when the reporting verb is in the past (said, told, asked).

DirectIndirectExample
Simple present (write/writes)Simple past (wrote)“I like tea.” → he liked tea
Present continuous (is writing)Past continuous (was writing)“I am reading.” → he was reading
Present perfect (has written)Past perfect (had written)“I have finished.” → he had finished
Present perfect continuousPast perfect continuous“I have been waiting.” → he had been waiting
Simple past (wrote)Past perfect (had written)“I saw him.” → she had seen him
Past continuous (was writing)Past perfect continuous (had been writing)“I was sleeping.” → he had been sleeping
Past perfectNo change“I had left.” → he had left
will / shallwould (shall → should when it means duty)“I will come.” → he would come
cancould“I can swim.” → he could swim
maymight“It may rain.” → it might rain
musthad to (obligation) or must (rule, certainty)“I must go.” → he had to go
could, would, should, might, ought toNo change“You should rest.” → I should rest

Correct: She said that she had not seen him at the station. Incorrect: She said that she hasn't seen him at the station.

concepts.title: When the tense does not change
concepts.body:
• Reporting verb in the present or future: He says, “I am busy.” → He says that he is busy. She will say, “I am ready.” → She will say that she is ready.
  • Universal truths and scientific facts: The teacher said, “The sun rises in the east.” → The teacher said that the sun rises in the east. He said, “Two and two make four.” → He said that two and two make four.
  • Proverbs and habitual facts: Father said, “Honesty is the best policy.” → Father said that honesty is the best policy.
  • Historical facts (simple past stays): He said, “Gandhiji was born in 1869.” → He said that Gandhiji was born in 1869.
  • Past perfect and the modals could, would, should, might, ought to stay as they are.

Trap: He says that two and two made four and He said that two and two made four are both wrong.

concepts.title: Pronoun changes: the SON rule
concepts.body:
Person in the quoteChanges to matchExample
First person (I, me, my, we, us, our)the Subject of the reporting verbRavi said, “I lost my pen.” → Ravi said that he had lost his pen.
Second person (you, your)the Object of the reporting verb (the listener)He said to me, “You are late.” → He told me that I was late.
Third person (he, she, it, they)No changeShe said, “He is honest.” → She said that he was honest.

Check gender and number carefully: Raghav said to Meera, “Are you upset with me?” → Raghav asked Meera if she was upset with him (not her). The French scientist said, “I want ...” → he/she wanted, never I wanted.

concepts.title: Time and place words
concepts.body:
DirectIndirect
nowthen
today, tonightthat day, that night
tomorrowthe next day / the following day
yesterdaythe previous day / the day before
last night, last weekthe previous night, the previous week
next week, next yearthe following week, the following year
agobefore
this, thesethat, those
herethere
thusso / in that way
comego (when the place changes)

These changes apply when the reported time or place is no longer the same. this used as a time word (this week) becomes that (that week).

concepts.title: Questions
concepts.body:
Reporting verb: asked, enquired of, wanted to know, wondered. The question becomes a statement: subject before verb, no do/does/did, no question mark.

Yes/no questions (start with a helping verb): use if or whether.

  • Meera said to her brother, “Have you finished your homework?” → Meera asked her brother if he had finished his homework.
  • He said to me, “Do you like music?” → He asked me if I liked music. (do disappears, like back-shifts)
  • He said, “Would you help me with this work?” → He asked if I would help him with that work.

Wh-questions: keep the question word, no if.

  • He said to me, “What time do the banks open and close?” → He asked me what time the banks opened and closed.
  • The stranger said to me, “Why did you leave so early?” → The stranger asked me why I had left so early.
CorrectIncorrect
She asked me where I lived.She asked me where did I live.
He asked if I was ready.He asked that was I ready.
He asked me what I wanted.He said me what I wanted.

concepts.title: Commands, requests and advice
concepts.body:
Pattern: reporting verb + listener + (not) to + V1. Choose the reporting verb by tone.

Tone in the quoteReporting verbExample
Orderordered, commanded, toldThe officer said to the guard, “Open the gate.” → The officer ordered the guard to open the gate.
Request (please, kindly)requested, askedShe said to him, “Please wait here.” → She requested him to wait there.
AdviceadvisedThe doctor said, “Don't eat oily food.” → The doctor advised the patient not to eat oily food.
WarningwarnedHe said, “Don't touch the wire.” → He warned me not to touch the wire.
Prohibitionforbade (no not)Father said, “Don't go out.” → Father forbade me to go out.

please disappears because requested already carries it. Negative commands use not to, never to not or don't. told to her to read and said me to open are wrong; write told her to read, told me to open.

concepts.title: Let's, let and suggestions
concepts.body:
• Let's / Let us as a proposal → suggested / proposed that + they/we + should + V1, or suggested + V-ing.
    He said, “Let's go for a walk.” → He suggested that they should go for a walk. / He proposed going for a walk.
  • Let asking permission → requested / asked to let / allow.
    He said to me, “Let me go home.” → He requested me to let him go home.
  • Let as a wish about someone else → wished / said that he might / should.
    The coach said, “Let the best team win.” → The coach wished that the best team might win.
  • Negative proposal: “Let's not waste time.” → He suggested that they should not waste time.

Incorrect: He suggested them to go for a walk. (suggest is never followed by object + to-infinitive.)

concepts.title: Exclamations, wishes and greetings
concepts.body:
Exclamations become statements with exclaimed with joy / sorrow / surprise / wonder, or cried out. Remove What a, How, Alas, Hurrah, Oh and use very or a very.

  • She said, “What a beautiful garden!” → She exclaimed with joy that it was a very beautiful garden.
  • He said, “Alas! I have lost my purse.” → He exclaimed with sorrow that he had lost his purse.
  • They said, “Hurrah! We have won the match.” → They exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
  • “How clever you are!” he said to her. → He exclaimed that she was very clever.

Wishes, prayers, greetings and thanks:

  • Mother said, “May God bless you!” → Mother prayed that God might bless me.
  • He said, “Good morning, sir.” → He wished his teacher good morning. or He respectfully greeted the teacher.
  • She said to me, “Thank you.” → She thanked me.
  • He said, “Good night, friends.” → He bade his friends good night.

concepts.title: Indirect to direct
concepts.body:
1. Turn the reporting verb back: told me → said to me,; asked → said to ..., with a question mark; ordered / requested → said to ..., with an imperative (add please for a request).
  2. Remove that / if / whether / to and put the exact words inside quotation marks.
  3. Move the tense one step forward (was → is, had seen → saw or have seen, would → will).
  4. Restore pronouns and time words from the speaker's point of view (the next day → tomorrow, there → here).
  • I asked Mary if she would lend me a pencil. → I said to Mary, “Will you lend me a pencil?”
  • The old man asked the boy where the postman was. → The old man said to the boy, “Where is the postman?”
  • She exclaimed with sorrow that life had become miserable. → She said, “Alas! Life has become miserable.”

concepts.title: Mixed and multiple sentences
concepts.body:
When the quote has two kinds of sentence, report each with its own verb and join them with and, and added that, or and asked.

  • He said to me, “I am going to the market. Will you come with me?” → He told me that he was going to the market and asked if I would come with him.
  • She said, “Alas! I am ruined. Please help me.” → She exclaimed with sorrow that she was ruined and requested me to help her.

Address words (sir, friends, my son) and yes / no answers are reported with verbs: He said, “Yes, sir, I will do it.” → He respectfully replied in the affirmative and said that he would do it.

varieties.name: Statements
varieties.how: said to → told, add that, change pronouns (SON), back-shift the tense, change time words.

example.q: Select the indirect form: She said to me, “I will visit my grandmother tomorrow.”
example.answer: She told me that she would visit her grandmother the next day.

varieties.name: When the tense does not change
varieties.how: Keep the tense if the reporting verb is present or future, or if the quote is a universal truth, proverb or habitual fact. Pronouns still change.

example.q: Select the indirect form: He said, “Two and two make four.”
steps: Reporting verb said is past, so normally the tense moves back.
But two and two make four is a universal truth.
example.answer: He said that two and two make four.

varieties.name: Yes or no questions
varieties.how: asked + if/whether + subject + verb. Drop do/does/did and the question mark; back-shift the tense.

example.q: Select the indirect form: Raghav said to Meera, “Are you upset with me?”
steps: Starts with Are, so it is a yes/no question: asked Meera if.
example.answer: Raghav asked Meera if she was upset with him.

varieties.name: Wh-questions
varieties.how: asked + question word + subject + verb. No if, no did, statement order.

example.q: Select the indirect form: The stranger said to me, “Why did you leave the room so early yesterday?”
steps: did you leave (simple past) → I had left (past perfect).
example.answer: The stranger asked me why I had left the room so early the previous day.

varieties.name: Commands, requests and advice
varieties.how: ordered / requested / advised + listener + (not) to + V1. Remove please; use not to for negatives.

example.q: Select the indirect form: The doctor said to the patient, “Please don't eat oily food.”
example.answer: The doctor advised the patient not to eat oily food.

varieties.name: Let's and suggestions
varieties.how: Let's → suggested/proposed that they should + V1. Let me → requested ... to let/allow.

example.q: Select the indirect form: He said to his friends, “Let's go to the cinema tonight.”
steps: Let's is a proposal: suggested to his friends that.
example.answer: He suggested to his friends that they should go to the cinema that night.

varieties.name: Exclamations, wishes and greetings
varieties.how: exclaimed with joy/sorrow/surprise that + statement with very; prayed that ... might; wished, greeted, thanked.

example.q: Select the indirect form: He said, “Alas! I have lost my purse.”
steps: Alas shows sorrow: exclaimed with sorrow that; remove Alas and the exclamation mark.
example.answer: He exclaimed with sorrow that he had lost his purse.

varieties.name: Indirect to direct
varieties.how: Reverse each change: told → said to, remove that/if/to, move the tense forward, restore pronouns and time words, add quotation marks.

example.q: Select the direct form: I asked Mary if she would lend me a pencil.
steps: asked Mary if → a yes/no question: I said to Mary, “...?”
Question order: Will you lend me a pencil?
example.answer: I said to Mary, “Will you lend me a pencil?”

tips: Decide the kind of sentence inside the quotes first: statement, yes/no question, wh-question, command, Let's, or exclamation. That fixes the reporting verb and connector.
Check pronouns before tenses. A wrong him/her or he/I removes options fastest.
In reported questions the subject comes before the verb: 'where she lived', not 'where did she live'.
Told always needs a listener (told me, told her); said never takes a direct object (said to me, not said me).
For commands, look for 'to + V1' and 'not to + V1'. Options with 'that he should' are rarely the answer for a plain command.
If the reporting verb is says or will say, do not change the tense at all.
Time words give quick eliminations: an option that keeps 'tomorrow', 'yesterday' or 'last night' after a past reporting verb is usually wrong.
traps: Universal truths and proverbs keep their present tense even after said: 'He said that the earth moves round the sun.'
Simple past and present perfect both become past perfect: 'I saw him' becomes 'she had seen him', not 'she saw him'.
Asked 'that' is wrong. Yes/no questions take if or whether; wh-questions take the question word itself.
Forbade already means 'told not to': 'He forbade me to go', not 'He forbade me not to go'.
With suggest, use 'suggested that they should go' or 'suggested going', never 'suggested them to go'.
After 'exclaimed', remove What/How and the exclamation mark; keep the statement order.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.
Rohan said, “I am tired.”
options: Rohan said that he is tired.
Rohan said that he was tired.
Rohan said that I was tired.
Rohan told that he had been tired.
questions.solution: Past reporting verb → am becomes was; I becomes he. Rohan said that he was tired.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.
The officer said to the guard, “Open the gate.”
options: The officer ordered the guard to open the gate.
The officer said the guard open the gate.
The officer ordered the guard that he opens the gate.
The officer asked the guard if he opened the gate.
questions.solution: A command becomes ordered + object + to + verb: The officer ordered the guard to open the gate.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.
Meera said to her brother, “Have you finished your homework?”
options: Meera asked her brother that had he finished his homework.
Meera asked her brother if he had finished his homework.
Meera asked her brother if he has finished his homework.
Meera told her brother whether had he finished his homework.
questions.solution: Yes/no question → asked … if. Statement order (he had), and present perfect have finished → past perfect had finished; your → his.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.
She said, “I will visit my grandmother tomorrow.”
options: She said that she will visit her grandmother tomorrow.
She said that she would visit her grandmother the next day.
She said that she would visit my grandmother the next day.
She said that she would have visited her grandmother the next day.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.
The stranger said to me, “Why did you leave the room so early yesterday?”
options: The stranger asked me why I had left the room so early the previous day.
The stranger asked me why did I leave the room so early the previous day.
The stranger asked me why I left the room so early yesterday.
The stranger told me why had I left the room so early the day before.
questions.solution: Wh-question → asked me why + statement order. did leave (past) → had left; yesterday → the previous day.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.
The doctor said to the patient, “Please don't eat oily food.”
options: The doctor requested the patient please not to eat oily food.
The doctor advised the patient not to eat oily food.
The doctor said to the patient that don't eat oily food.
The doctor advised the patient to not eating oily food.
questions.solution: Advice/request with don't → advised/requested + object + not to + verb. Please is dropped because the reporting verb carries the politeness.

flashcards.back: the next day / the previous day / then

flashcards.front: When does the tense NOT change?
flashcards.back: Reporting verb in present tense, or a universal truth / habitual fact.
He suggested that they should go. (or: He proposed going.)

flashcards.front: Indirect: past simple and present perfect

flashcards.back: told/asked + object + not to + V1: He told me not to shout.
